name: Environmental Geology
notes: Six courses total: one or both introductory courses plus four or five electives.
Intended especially for natural-science and social-science concentrators planning further study or employment in environmental fields.
EESC 205 (Solid Earth Geophysics) is an acceptable substitute for EESC 215.
See the department's major/minor course overlap policy.

requirementGroups.label: One or both introductory courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Required Courses. One or both of the following introductory courses: EESC 101: Introduction to Earth Sciences; EESC 103: Introduction to Environmental Science

requirementGroups.label: Five environmental geology electives
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Four or five of the following elective courses: EESC 105: Introduction to Climate Change; EESC 201: Evolution of the Earth; EESC 203: Sedimentology and Stratigraphy; EESC 204: Earth Materials; EESC 208: Structural Geology; EESC 211: Nature's Fury; EESC 212: A Climate Change Perspective to Chemical Oceanography; EESC 213: Hydrology and Water Resources; EESC 215: Environmental and Applied Geophysics (EESC 205: Solid Earth Geophysics is an acceptable substitute); EESC 216: Environmental Geochemistry; EESC 218: Atmospheric Chemistry; EESC 219: Energy and Society; EESC 252: Marine Geology
requirementGroups.note: Take five electives if you took one introductory course, four if you took both.
